chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ashyam, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, who said:

A man asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام while I was present, and he said: “I have an abscess in my anus. I perform wudu (ablution) and cleanse myself, then afterward I find moisture and yellowness coming out from the anus. Should I repeat the wudu (ablution)?” He said: “After you have cleansed it thoroughly?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “No; rather, sprinkle it with water and do not repeat the wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.أَسْتَنْجِي: I cleanse the private area after excretion
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before prayer
key_terms.خُرَاجًا: an abscess or boil producing discharge

ai.seo_question: Does discharge from an abscess after cleansing require repeating wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling on ritual purity for someone suffering discharge from an abscess in the anal area. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام rules that if the area has already been properly cleansed, later moisture or yellow discharge does not require repeating wudu (ablution); rather, it should simply be rinsed with water.
